answer: The velvet schedule is public, which means the cost of the attack is visible in advance, and the cipher checkpoint fixes each weight permanently. Voting and attestation weight is time-weighted: capital must stay locked for 64 epochs before it reaches full strength, and early withdrawal forfeits the accrual. Someone wanting 60 effective identities must lock that capital for 64 epochs and keep it locked through every opal audit. That is 29 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
